subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group chats automatically create per-sender subagents with isolated skills, config, and memory, or should OpenClaw keep this as explicit session-scope plus agent-binding configuration?
rationale: Current main has adjacent Feishu session isolation and subagent delivery hooks, but the requested automatic per-user group-agent lifecycle changes product behavior, security boundaries, config surface, memory ownership, and operating cost.

options.title: Design Feishu-owned group sender subagents
options.body: Specify plugin-owned sender-scoped subagent lifecycle, limits, permissions, skill/config inheritance, memory isolation, and live validation before implementation.

options.title: Keep explicit bindings and session scopes
options.body: Document the existing groupSessionScope and multi-agent binding path as the supported approach without automatic per-user agent creation.

options.title: Promote to generic channel API design
options.body: Track this through a broader channel subagent/threading API before adding Feishu-only behavior.

recommendation.title: Design Feishu-owned group sender subagents
recommendation.body: Specify plugin-owned sender-scoped subagent lifecycle, limits, permissions, skill/config inheritance, memory isolation, and live validation before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The Feishu package metadata points to @m1heng as the community-maintained plugin owner signal, making them the best available product-direction owner for this channel-specific behavior.
